evidence.claim: In 2022 Mexico recorded 696 attacks against the press, 12 journalists were murdered, 42.53% of documented attacks were perpetrated directly by state actors, and the executive branch made 176 stigmatizing comments against media, journalists, and civil society.
evidence.title: Mexico: Voices Against Indifference
evidence.excerpt: In 2022 Mexico recorded 696 attacks against the press, 12 journalists were murdered, 42.53% of documented attacks were perpetrated directly by state actors, and the executive branch made 176 stigmatizing comments against media, journalists, and civil society.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Specialist annual report with quantified 2022 documentation and clear methodology.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirect but strong: captures AMLO-era executive behavior and state-actor conduct in 2022.
contrary_evidence: Not every attack was personally ordered by the president.
Some violence was also driven by criminal actors rather than the federal executive.

evidence.claim: UN human-rights staff said leaked Sedena documents or a government-acquired software package revealed illicit surveillance against journalists and human-rights defenders, calling it grave, intimidating, and contrary to a safe environment for criticism.
evidence.title: La ONU-DH expresa su preocupación por actos de vigilancia ilícita contra personas defensoras de derechos humanos y periodistas
evidence.excerpt: UN human-rights staff said leaked Sedena documents or a government-acquired software package revealed illicit surveillance against journalists and human-rights defenders, calling it grave, intimidating, and contrary to a safe environment for criticism.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official UN country-office statement with explicit concern about government-linked surveillance.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirect but strong: it implicates federal authorities and the armed forces under AMLO.
contrary_evidence: The statement is not itself a court finding of personal presidential orders.
It addresses surveillance/intimidation more than kinetic violence.

evidence.claim: AMLO said his administration would send a constitutional electoral-reform proposal to Congress to guarantee clean and free elections and to leave behind electoral fraud.
evidence.title: 28.04.22 Versión estenográfica de la conferencia de prensa matutina del presidente Andrés Manuel López Obrador
evidence.excerpt: AMLO said his administration would send a constitutional electoral-reform proposal to Congress to guarantee clean and free elections and to leave behind electoral fraud.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct presidential transcript, but the claim is the ruler's own framing of a politically contested reform.
evidence.period_fit: Direct 2022 conduct and justification for changing electoral rules.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to AMLO as the initiator of the reform package.
contrary_evidence: Critics argued the reform would weaken electoral independence rather than protect it.
The source is self-justifying and does not prove the reform would actually improve democracy.

evidence.claim: AMLO said the accusation that the reform sought his reelection was false and that the reform did not propose presidential reelection.
evidence.title: 16.11.22 Versión estenográfica de la conferencia de prensa matutina del presidente Andrés Manuel López Obrador
evidence.excerpt: AMLO said the accusation that the reform sought his reelection was false and that the reform did not propose presidential reelection.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct ruler statement in an official transcript, but embedded in a partisan information campaign.
evidence.period_fit: Direct 2022 statement about transfer rules and succession.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to AMLO's own public position.
contrary_evidence: The same transcript also promotes a broad electoral overhaul that critics said would weaken independent institutions.
Self-denial is not independent proof of future compliance.

evidence.claim: INE completed the 2022 recall count, reporting 17.77% participation and 91.86% for López Obrador to stay in office; the INE leadership described the day as a free, secret, peaceful civic exercise.
evidence.title: Realiza INE declaratoria de resultados del proceso de Revocación de Mandato
evidence.excerpt: INE completed the 2022 recall count, reporting 17.77% participation and 91.86% for López Obrador to stay in office; the INE leadership described the day as a free, secret, peaceful civic exercise.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous official election administrator record with exact vote totals and procedural description.
evidence.period_fit: Direct 2022 ruler-period evidence of contestability and transfer rules.
evidence.ruler_attribution: AMLO was the sitting president subjected to the legally organized recall process; the source shows the institution ran and counted the vote, not that he created the rules.
contrary_evidence: The result was non-binding because participation fell well short of the 40% legal threshold.
A recall is not the same as a full competitive general election.

evidence.claim: Mexico's lower house rejected AMLO's controversial electoral reform after critics said it could undermine the country's electoral independence.
evidence.title: Mexican Congress rejects president's electoral reform bid
evidence.excerpt: Mexico's lower house rejected AMLO's controversial electoral reform after critics said it could undermine the country's electoral independence.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters reporting on a contemporaneous legislative defeat and the stated criticism of the proposal.
evidence.period_fit: Direct 2022 evidence of conflict over electoral independence.
evidence.ruler_attribution: The reform was backed by López Obrador, but the institutional rejection came from Congress, not from him alone.
contrary_evidence: The bill failed in Congress, so the executive did not fully capture the electoral rules in 2022.
Reuters frames the concern as critics' assessment, not a judicial finding.

evidence.claim: AMLO's daily morning briefings had become hostile to parts of the media; in July 2021 he added a 'Who's Who' segment that singles out journalists and publications, and the report says he classifies media into 'good' and 'bad'.
evidence.title: Mexico | Reuters Institute for the Study of Journalism
evidence.publisher: Reuters Institute for the Study of Journalism
evidence.excerpt: AMLO's daily morning briefings had become hostile to parts of the media; in July 2021 he added a 'Who's Who' segment that singles out journalists and publications, and the report says he classifies media into 'good' and 'bad'.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Oxford-based research summary describing the president's public communication pattern and media treatment.
evidence.period_fit: Directly relevant to 2022 information environment and ruler conduct in office.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to AMLO's own communications style and public briefings.
contrary_evidence: The report is descriptive rather than legal; it does not by itself establish formal censorship or state orders.
Mexico still had plural media outlets and criticism remained public.

evidence.claim: ARTICLE 19 reported 696 attacks against the press in Mexico in 2022, 12 journalists murdered, 42.53% of documented attacks perpetrated directly by state actors, and 176 stigmatizing executive comments against the media, journalists, and civil-society organizations.
evidence.title: Mexico: Voices Against Indifference
evidence.excerpt: ARTICLE 19 reported 696 attacks against the press in Mexico in 2022, 12 journalists murdered, 42.53% of documented attacks perpetrated directly by state actors, and 176 stigmatizing executive comments against the media, journalists, and civil-society organizations.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Annual monitoring report with explicit 2022 counts and attribution categories.
evidence.period_fit: Retrospective but directly about 2022 conduct and environment.
evidence.ruler_attribution: The report ties the pattern to the current administration's public discourse and media ecosystem, but not every attack is personally ordered by AMLO.
contrary_evidence: The report is about documented attacks, not every unreported incident.
Some attacks were subnational or non-federal, so presidential attribution is partial.

evidence.claim: R3D and Citizen Lab found that Mexican journalists and a human rights defender were infected with Pegasus between 2019 and 2021, after Mexico's president had assured the public the government no longer used the spyware and that there would be no further abuses.
evidence.title: New Pegasus Spyware Abuses Identified in Mexico
evidence.excerpt: R3D and Citizen Lab found that Mexican journalists and a human rights defender were infected with Pegasus between 2019 and 2021, after Mexico's president had assured the public the government no longer used the spyware and that there would be no further abuses.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Technical forensic validation by a university lab, with explicit limits on attribution to a particular customer.
evidence.period_fit: Target-period relevant because the infections span into the AMLO years and were publicly reported in 2022.
evidence.ruler_attribution: The source places the infections during AMLO's government and after his public assurance, but does not identify the specific customer or direct order giver.
contrary_evidence: The lab explicitly says it could not attribute the hacking to a particular NSO customer.
The infections span 2019-2021, so the source is only partly target-year specific.

evidence.claim: The UN human-rights office said illicit surveillance against journalists and human-rights defenders constituted arbitrary interference, came to light through leaked Sedena documents or a government-acquired software package, and had an intimidating effect that signaled intolerance of criticism.
evidence.title: La ONU-DH expresa su preocupación por actos de vigilancia ilícita contra personas defensoras de derechos humanos y periodistas
evidence.excerpt: The UN human-rights office said illicit surveillance against journalists and human-rights defenders constituted arbitrary interference, came to light through leaked Sedena documents or a government-acquired software package, and had an intimidating effect that signaled intolerance of criticism.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official UN human-rights statement issued contemporaneously in Mexico with direct normative assessment.
evidence.period_fit: Direct 2022 evidence about the ruler-period information environment and state surveillance concerns.
evidence.ruler_attribution: The statement concerns state institutions under the AMLO government, but does not directly name the top-level order giver.
contrary_evidence: The UN note stops short of naming AMLO personally as the person who ordered surveillance.
It is a human-rights concern statement, not a court finding.

unresolved_gaps: Direct 2022 evidence on AMLO's personal control over civilian-nuclear safety appointments, regulatory discipline, or command-side decisions is thin.
There is no Mexico-originating war, proxy conflict, or coercive peace leverage in 2022, so the dossier is mostly diplomatic posture rather than operational conflict conduct.
Specific chain-of-command evidence for some police, military, and intelligence abuses remains incomplete, especially for local versus federal responsibility.
Some of the evidence about electoral reform and media pressure is rhetorical or journalistic rather than a direct legal finding of intent to entrench power.
The causal split between AMLO policy, inherited weakness, and global shocks is still only partially recoverable for 2022 poverty, inflation, and investment outcomes.
Independent post-launch quality and outcome audits for IMSS-Bienestar, education recovery, and related welfare programs are thinner than the rollout record.
Direct documentary evidence of personal enrichment, hidden financial benefit, or knowing approval of surveillance remains limited.
Durability and post-launch independent audits for AIFA, Dos Bocas, IMSS-Bienestar, and the education programs are thinner than the implementation record.
